boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission places and self-guided activities on or near Princeton’s campus.

cards.title: Browse the Art Museum galleries
cards.subtitle: Princeton University Campus
cards.notes: Meet at the museum and choose a gallery to explore together; admission is free to all visitors during posted museum hours.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission gallery visit with changing exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Princeton University Art Museum states that it is free to all and lists public visiting hours.
cards.access_notes: Use the museum’s posted hours; it is closed on several listed holidays.

cards.title: See contemporary art at Bainbridge House
cards.subtitle: 158 Nassau Street, Princeton
cards.notes: Step into the historic Bainbridge House for the current gallery exhibition, then continue your walk along Nassau Street.
cards.short_summary: A free downtown gallery stop in a colonial-era house.
cards.evidence_claim: Art@Bainbridge states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: The gallery lists limited hours: Friday–Sunday; check the official page before going.

cards.entity_name: Bookscape at the Cotsen Children's Library
cards.title: Read beneath Bookscape’s bonsai tree
cards.subtitle: Firestone Library
cards.notes: Bring a friend or a book and spend time in Bookscape, the public gallery’s whimsical reading environment with a two-story bonsai tree.
cards.short_summary: A free public reading space inside Firestone Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Library says Bookscape is open to the public and free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Cotsen Children's Library Public Gallery; follow Firestone visitor procedures.

cards.title: Pause in the University Chapel
cards.subtitle: Next to Firestone Library and Washington Road
cards.notes: Visit for quiet conversation, reflection, or a few minutes of looking at the architecture; people of all faiths are welcome.
cards.short_summary: A daily open chapel for prayer, meditation, and quiet time.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton Religious Life says the chapel is open 7 a.m.–11 p.m. and welcomes people of all faiths for prayer and meditation.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.; follow the University visitor policy.

cards.title: Picnic in Morven’s historic garden
cards.subtitle: 55 Stockton Street, Princeton
cards.notes: Pack food from home, claim a bench or table, and use the interpretive signs to guide an unhurried walk through the grounds.
cards.short_summary: Five acres of historic gardens with seating and interpretation.
cards.evidence_claim: Morven states that its garden is open daily from sunrise to sunset and free to all.
cards.access_notes: Garden access is daily from sunrise to sunset; this applies to the garden, not necessarily museum-house admission.

cards.title: Take a picnic walk at Princeton Battlefield
cards.subtitle: 500 Mercer Road, Princeton
cards.notes: Use the designated picnic area for a bring-your-own snack, then take a daylight walk through this state historic landscape.
cards.short_summary: A nearby state-park picnic and walking destination.
cards.evidence_claim: New Jersey State Parks lists Princeton Battlefield State Park as open daily sunrise to sunset with no entrance fee.
cards.source_title: Picnicking | New Jersey State Parks, Forests & Historic Sites
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset; the state page lists no entrance fee.

cards.entity_name: Cannon Green and the Big Cannon
cards.title: Find the Big Cannon behind Nassau Hall
cards.subtitle: Princeton University main campus
cards.notes: Make the Big Cannon your meet-up landmark, then read its campus history and take a relaxed loop through the surrounding green.
cards.short_summary: A campus landmark with a documented Revolutionary War story.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton Archives identifies the Big Cannon as buried in the center of Cannon Green behind Nassau Hall.
cards.access_notes: Princeton states that its campus is always open to families for strolling and outdoor exploration.

cards.title: Take the circular path through Prospect Garden
cards.subtitle: Princeton University main campus
cards.notes: Walk the garden’s paths at an easy pace, pause by the fountain, and use the benches for a no-plan catch-up outdoors.
cards.short_summary: A campus garden with paths, benches, and a fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton Admission describes Prospect Garden’s paths, fountain, benches, and everyday walking use.
cards.source_title: Places on Campus: Prospect Garden | Princeton Admission
cards.access_notes: Princeton says its campus is always open to families for strolling through gardens and outdoor spaces.

cards.title: Meet at the tigers outside Nassau Hall
cards.subtitle: Princeton University main campus
cards.notes: Use the tiger statues as a photo and meeting point, then continue on foot through the historic core of campus together.
cards.short_summary: A named Nassau Hall landmark on an open campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton identifies the tigers guarding Nassau Hall as part of campus exploration and says campus is always open to families for strolling.
cards.source_title: University offers year-round programming for families, children
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus stop; follow current University visitor policies.

cards.title: Make your own outdoor art walk
cards.subtitle: Main Campus, beginning near Nassau Hall
cards.notes: Start near Nassau Hall and use the museum’s online campus-art resources to choose a few outdoor works to discuss together.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided route through Princeton’s outdoor art collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Princeton University Art Museum says groups are welcome to explore campus art on their own and provides online collection resources.
cards.source_title: Group Visits | Princeton University Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Keep the route outdoors and use the museum’s online resources; campus strolling is described by Princeton as always open to families.
